name: LIFE (Eclipse)
question: Among women with fecal incontinence, how often could the Eclipse vaginal bowel-control system be fitted and reduce leakage episodes during short-term use?

design.population: Women at six clinical sites with at least four fecal incontinence episodes on a two-week baseline diary underwent attempted device fitting.
design.description: Multicenter prospective open-label single-arm device study

verdictNote: One-month response was measured among women who could be fitted; 49/110 did not enter treatment.
takeaway: In the single-arm LIFE study, Eclipse could be fitted in 61/110 women; 48/61 treated women had at least 50% fewer fecal incontinence episodes at one month. There was no comparator arm.

reports.label: One-month pivotal report
reports.dateLocator: Crossref published-print: March 2015; PubMed journal issue: March 2015; online day unverified
reports.citation: Richter HE, Matthews CA, Muir T, et al. "A Vaginal Bowel-Control System for the Treatment of Fecal Incontinence." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2015;125(3):540-547. doi:10.1097/AOG.0000000000000639
reports.followUp: One month of treatment, with an optional two-month extension

results.measure: At least 50% fewer episodes at one month among successfully fitted women entering treatment (intention to treat)
results.note: The abstract reports P<0.001 but does not state a prespecified success threshold or hypothesis.

results.measure: At least 50% fewer episodes at one month among women with a valid treatment diary (per protocol)
results.note: Five fitted participants lacked a valid one-month diary.

results.measure: At least 50% fewer episodes at three months among women assessed after the optional extension
results.note: Optional extension; 44 women had a three-month assessment.

results.measure: Bowel symptoms rated very much or much better at one month among women with a valid diary

harms.label: Serious adverse events
harms.note: No serious adverse events were reported across fitting and treatment.

delivery.label: Successful fit and treatment entry
delivery.value: 61/110 women (55.5%) were successfully fitted and entered treatment.

delivery.label: Optional extension assessment
delivery.value: 44 women were assessed at three months after an optional two-month extension.

reports.label: Bowel-function analysis
reports.dateLocator: Crossref published-print: February 2016; PubMed journal issue: February 2016; online day unverified
reports.citation: Varma MG, Matthews CA, Muir T, et al. "Impact of a Novel Vaginal Bowel Control System on Bowel Function." *Dis Colon Rectum.* 2016;59(2):127-131. doi:10.1097/DCR.0000000000000517
reports.followUp: One month of treatment in 56 evaluable women
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract, Patients and Main Outcome Measures

results.measure: Mean proportion of bowel movements associated with urgency, baseline to one month
results.note: Within-cohort secondary analysis of 56 evaluable women; the abstract gives no bowel-movement denominator.

results.measure: Proportion of bowel movements with Bristol stool form 6 or 7, baseline to one month
results.note: Within-cohort secondary analysis; the abstract gives no bowel-movement denominator.

delivery.label: Device configuration
delivery.value: Vaginal insert with a pressure-regulated pump.

reports.label: Fitting-predictor analysis
reports.dateLocator: Crossref published-print: September 2016; PubMed journal issue: September–October 2016; online day unverified
reports.citation: Matthews CA, Varma MG, Takase-Sanchez MM, et al. "Characteristics Associated With Successful Fitting of a Vaginal Bowel Control System for Fecal Incontinence." *Female Pelvic Med Reconstr Surg.* 2016;22(5):359-363. doi:10.1097/SPV.0000000000000290

results.endpoint: Successful fitting and prior prolapse surgery
results.measure: Adjusted odds of successful fit without versus with prior prolapse surgery
results.note: Prior prolapse surgery was associated with fitting failure; observational predictor analysis.

results.measure: Adjusted odds of successful fit per additional centimeter of vaginal length
results.note: Shorter vaginal length was associated with fitting failure; observational predictor analysis.
